translationRepairs: His great-great-grandfather Xiqi served as staff merit officer in Huzhou.
His great-grandfather Xiqi served as staff merit officer in Huzhou.
曾祖 is the father's grandfather (great-grandfather). The genealogical sequence 曾祖 / 祖 / 父 confirms the original 'great-great-grandfather' is one generation too remote.
His great-grandfather Hongqing was prefect of Suzhou.
His grandfather Hongqing was prefect of Suzhou.
After 曾祖, 祖 names the grandfather. Rendering 祖宏慶 as great-grandfather collapses two generations.

During the Tang Tianyou era Zhuangzong was establishing his headquarters and eagerly sought talented men. By special edict he appointed Qi military adjutant of Daizhou. When his term ended Qi returned to Taiyuan, where Military Commissioner Zhang Chengye admired his character and treated him with exceptional regard.

During the Tang Tianyou era Zhuangzong was establishing his headquarters and eagerly sought talented men. By special edict he appointed Qi military adjutant of Daizhou. When his term ended Qi returned to Taiyuan, where Army Supervisor Zhang Chengye admired his character and treated him with exceptional regard.
監軍使 is an army supervisor, not a jiedushi (節度使) military commissioner.
When Gaozu entered Luoyang he did not reproach him, but only reassigned him as director of the Secretariat.
When Gaozu entered Luoyang he did not reproach him, but only reassigned him as director of the Palace Library.
秘書監 is director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat (中書).
He rose through successive posts as vice minister of rites, justice, revenue, and war, attaining the rank of Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Bright Hall and the title Baron of a Founding State.

He rose through successive posts as vice minister of rites, justice, revenue, and war, attaining the rank of Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Bright Hall and the title Viscount of a Founding State.
開國子 is a founding-fief viscount (子); baron is 男.
His great-great-grandfather Xiqi was Merit Officer on the staff of Huzhou.
His great-grandfather Xiqi was Merit Officer on the staff of Huzhou.
The literal repeats the same 曾祖 error: Xiqi is Yao Yi's great-grandfather, not great-great-grandfather.
His great-grandfather Hongqing was Prefect of Suzhou.
His grandfather Hongqing was Prefect of Suzhou.
The literal likewise misreads 祖 as great-grandfather; in this sequence it is grandfather.
Liang Wenju, courtesy name Deyi, was a native of Yanzhou.
Liang Wenju, courtesy name Deyi, was a native of Yunzhou.
鄆州 is Yunzhou. Yanzhou is 兗州, which the chapter uses separately.
Liang Wenju, style name Deyi, was a man of Yanzhou.
Liang Wenju, style name Deyi, was a man of Yunzhou.
The literal has the same 鄆州/Yanzhou confusion; the place is Yunzhou.
When Youzhang governed Yanzhou he recommended Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng. When he transferred his command to Xuzhou he took Wenju on as an aide.
When Youzhang governed Yunzhou he recommended Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng. When he transferred his command to Xuzhou he took Wenju on as an aide.
友璋領鄆州 means he held Yunzhou, not Yanzhou.

Zhuangzong had sent Mingzong to seize Yanzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were there, and overnight he was cut off from them with no word of their fate. Filial longing burned in him, and he made his way back to Yan by a hidden route, then presented himself to Zhuangzong.

Zhuangzong had sent Mingzong to seize Yunzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were there, and overnight he was cut off from them with no word of their fate. Filial longing burned in him, and he made his way back to Yun by a hidden route, then presented himself to Zhuangzong.
襲據鄆州, 父母在鄆, and 歸鄆 all refer to Yunzhou, distinct from 兗州 in the previous unit.
When Youzhang held Yanzhou he memorialized Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng; when he moved his command to Xuzhou he recruited him as aide.
When Youzhang held Yunzhou he memorialized Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng; when he moved his command to Xuzhou he recruited him as aide.
The literal repeats 鄆州 as Yanzhou; Youzhang held Yunzhou.

At that time Zhuangzong sent Mingzong to seize Yanzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were in Yan; suddenly cut off, he did not know whether they lived or died. Filial feeling burned in him like fire, and he took a secret route back to Yan, then soon presented himself to Zhuangzong.

At that time Zhuangzong sent Mingzong to seize Yunzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were in Yun; suddenly cut off, he did not know whether they lived or died. Filial feeling burned in him like fire, and he took a secret route back to Yun, then soon presented himself to Zhuangzong.
The literal likewise substitutes Yan for 鄆; the city and prefecture are Yunzhou.

釋褐 means doffing commoner's clothes to take office, not leaving official robes. The proposed parenthetical gloss is unnecessary in the literal line.

維翰 here is later called 桑公; the examinee is Sang Weihan, not a Pei.
